entries.chapterTitle: To the one who seeks to be a true religious
entries.textEn: If any Religious desires to attain in a short time to holy recollection, spiritual silence, detachment, and poverty of spirit -- where the peaceful rest of the spirit is enjoyed, and union with God attained ; if he desires to be delivered from all the difficulties which created things put in his way, to be defended against all the wiles and illusions of Satan, and to be protected against himself, he must strictly practise the following instructions. If he will do this, with but ordinary attention, without other efforts or other practices, at the same time carefully observing what his rule prescribes, he will advance rapidly to great perfection, acquire all virtues in succession, and attain unto holy peace. All the evils to which the soul is subject proceed from three sources : the world, the devil, and the flesh. If we can hide ourselves from these we shall have no combats to fight. The world is less difficult, and the devil more difficult, to understand ; but the flesh is the most obstinate of all, and the last to be overcome together with the * old man.' If we do not conquer the three, we shall never conquer one ; and if we conquer one, we shall also conquer the others in the same proportion.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the world — First caution
entries.textEn: The first is, preserve an equal love and an equal forgetfulness of all men whether relatives or not : withdraw your affections from the former as well as from the latter, yea even rather more from the former, on account of the ties of blood, for fear lest the natural affections, which men always feel for their kindred, should thereby revive again. You must mortify this affection if you are to attain unto spiritual perfection. Look upon your kindred as strangers, and you Vill thereby the more completely discharge the obligations which they impose upon you ; for by not withdrawing your heart from God on their account, you will fulfil your duties towards them better by not giving to them those affections which are due unto God. Do not love one man more than another, for if you do you will fall into error. He whom God loves most is the most worthy of love, and you do not know who he is. But if you labour to forget all men alike -- as holy recollection requires you to do -- you will escape all error, whether great or small. Do not think about them; have nothing to say about them either good or bad. Avoid them as much, as you possibly can. If you do not observe this, as things go, you never will become a good religious, you will never attain to holy recollection, nor will you get rid of your imperfections. If you will indulge yourself here, Satan will in some way or other delude you, or you will delude yourself under the pretence of good or evil. If you will observe this direction you will be safe ; and in no other way will you ever get rid of the imperfections and escape the evils which result to your soul from intercourse with men.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the world — Second caution
entries.textEn: The second caution against the world relates to temporal goods. If you desire in earnest to escape the evils which worldly goods occasion, and restrain your excessive desires, you must hold all personal possession in abhorrence, and cast from you every thought about it. You must not be solicitous about what you eat or drink or wear, or about any created thing whatever : you must not be ' solicitous for to-morrow,' but occupy yourself with higher things -- with the Kingdom of God, that is, fidelity unto Him -- than with all these things which, as He says in the Gospel, ' shall be added unto you.' * He who takes care of the beasts of the field will not forget you. If you do this you will attain unto silence, and have peace in your senses.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the world — Third caution
entries.textEn: The third caution is most necessary, that you may avoid all evil in relation to the other Religious of the Community. Many persons from not heeding this have not only lost their peace of mind, but have also fallen, and fall daily, into great disorders and sin. Be especially careful never to let your mind dwell upon, still less your tongue to speak of, what is passing in the Community, its past or its present state. Do not speak of any Religious in particular, do not discuss his condition or his conversation, or anything that belongs to him, however important, either under the cloak of zeal, or of remedying what seems amiss, except only to him who of right should be spoken to, and then at the fitting time. Never be scandalised or surprised at what you see or hear, and labour to preserve yourself in complete oblivion of all. If you lived among the Angels and gave heed to what was going on, many things would * S. Matth. vi. 33. goods. House. Lot's wite. may enter. Satan. seem to you not to be good, because you do not understand them. Take warning from the example of Lot's wife who, because she was disturbed at the destruction of Sodom, looked back to behold it. God punished her for this, and she * was turned into a pillar of salt'* This teaches you that it is the will of God, even if you were living among devils, you should so live as not to turn back in thought to consider what they are doing, but forget them utterly. You are to keep your soul in purity before God, and not to suffer the thought of this or that to disturb you. Be sure of this, there is no lack of stumbling blocks in religious houses, because there is no lack of devils who are always labouring to throw down the saints. God permits this in order to try them and to prove them, and if you will not take care of yourself by observing this caution, you will never become a true Religious, do what, you may, neither will you attain to holy detachment and recollection, or escape the evils I am speaking of. If you live otherwise, in spite of your zeal and good intentions, Satan will lay hold of you in one way or another, and indeed you are already sufficiently in his power, when your soul is allowed such distractions as this. Remember those words of the Apostle, € If any man think himself to be religious, not bridling his tongue, this man's religion is vain.'f This is applicable to the interior, quite as much as to the exterior, tongue -- to thoughts as well as words. from the devil in Religion. If you wish to escape from Satan in Religion, you must give heed to thre$ things, without which you cannot be in safety from his cunning. In the first place I would have you take this general advice, which you should never forget, Ught* namely, that it is the ordinary practice of Satan to deceive those who are going on unto perfection by an appearance of good : he does not tempt them by what seems to be evil. He knows that they will scarcely regard that which they know to be wrong. You must therefore continually distrust that which seems to be good, and especially when obedience does not intervene. The remedy here is to take the advice of him who has authority to give it. This then is the.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the devil — First caution
entries.textEn: Never set about anything, however good and charitable it may seem, either to yourself or to any other, whether in the Community or out of it, except under obedience, unless you are bound to do it by the rule of your Order. If you do this you will acquire merit, and be in security ; you will be safe against yourself and against evil ; you will also avoid evils of which you are ignorant, and of which God will require an account one day. If you do not observe this caution in little things as well as in great, notwithstanding your apparent success, Satan will most certainly deceive you little or much. Even if your whole error consist in your not being guided in everything by obedience, you are plainly wrong, because God wills obedience rather than sacrifice,* and the actions of a Religious are not his own, but those of obedience, and if he withdraws them from the control of obedience, he will have to give account of them as lost.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the devil — Second caution
entries.textEn: The second caution is one very necessary, because the devil interferes exceedingly in the matter to which it refers. The observance of it brings great gain and profit, and the neglect of it loss and ruin. Never look upon your superior, be he who he may, otherwise than if you were looking upon God, in Whose place he stands. Keep a careful watch over yourself in this matter, and do not reflect upon the character, ways, or conversation, or habits of your superior. If you do, you will injure yourself, and you will change your obedience from divine into human, and you will be influenced by what you see in your superior, and not by the Invisible God whom you should obey in him. Your obedience will be in vain, or the more barren the more you are troubled by the untowardness, or the more you are pleased by the favour, of your superior. I tell you that a great many Religious in the way of perfection have been ruined by not looking upon their superiors as they ought to have done ; their obedience was almost worthless in the eyes of God, because it was influenced by human considerations. Unless you force yourself therefore to be indifferent as to who your superior may be, so far as your private feelings go, you will never be spiritual, neither will you faithfully observe your vows.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the devil — Third caution
entries.textEn: The third caution directed against Satan is this : strive with all your heart after humility in thought, word, and work, taking more pleasure in others than in yourself, wishing to see them in all things preferred to yourself, and this too with all your power from a sincere heart. In this way you will overcome evil with good, drive the devil away, and have joy in your heart. Labour to do this with respect to those who are less agreeable to you; for be assured, if you do not, you will never have true charity nor make progress in it. Be always more ready to receive instruction than to give it, even to the least of your brethren.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the flesh — First caution
entries.textEn: If you wish to be delivered from the uneasiness and imperfections which present themselves before you, in the habits and conversation of the Religious, and profit by what may occur, you must keep in mind that you entered the Community only to be mortified and tried, and that all the inmates of it are there, as in truth is the case, for the express purpose of trying you. Some mortify you by words, others by works, and others by thoughts ; in all this you are to submit yourself, unresisting as a statue to the polisher, the painter, and the gilder of it. If you do not, you will never be able to live as you ought with the Religious of your House ; you will not have holy peace, nor will you deliver yourself from much evil.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the flesh — Second caution
entries.textEn: Never omit any practices, if they are such as befit you, because they are disagreeable; neither observe them, on account of the pleasure which results from them, unless they be as necessary as those which are not agreeable. Otherwise you will find it impossible to acquire firmness, and conquer your weakness.

entries.chapterTitle: Against the flesh — Third caution
entries.textEn: In all your spiritual exercises never set your eyes upon the sweetness of them so as to cling to it, but embrace rather that in them which is unpleasant and troublesome. If you do not observe this rule, you will never destroy self love, nor acquire the love of God.

entries.chapterTitle: Prologue
entries.textEn: O my God, sweetness and joy of my heart, behold my soul for love of Thee will occupy itself with these maxims of love and light. For though the words thereof are mine, I have not the meaning and the power, and these are more pleasing to Thee than the language and the knowledge thereof. Nevertheless, O Lord, it may be that some may be drawn by them to serve and love Thee, and profit where I fail: that will be a consolation to me, if through me Thou shalt find in others what Thou canst not find in me. O my Lord, Thou lovest discretion, and light, and love, more than all the other operations of the soul; so then let these maxims furnish discretion to the wayfarer, enlighten him by the way, and supply him with motives of love for his journey. Away, then, with the rhetoric of this world, sounding words and the dry eloquence of human wisdom, weak and delusive, never pleasing unto Thee. Let us speak to the heart words flowing with sweetness and love, and such as Thou delightest in. Thou wilt be pleased herein, O my God, and it may be that Thou wilt also remove the hindrance and the stones of stumbling from before many souls who fall through ignorance, and who for want of light wander out of the right way, though they think they are walking in it, and following the footsteps of Thy most sweet Son Jesus Christ our Lord, and imitating His life, estate, and virtues according to the rule of detachment and of spiritual poverty. But, O Father of mercy, do Thou give us this grace, for without Thee, O Lord, we shall do nothing. IMITATION OF CHBIST.

entries.chapterTitle: There is no progress but in the imitation of Christ, who is the Way,
entries.textEn: There is no progress but in the imitation of Christ, who is the Way, the Truth, and the Life, and the Gate by which he who will be saved must enter. Every spirit, therefore, that will walk in sweetness at its ease, shunning the imitation of Christ, is, in my opinion, nothing worth.

entries.chapterTitle: Your first care must be to be anxiously and lovingly earnest in your
entries.textEn: Your first care must be to be anxiously and lovingly earnest in your endeavours to imitate Christ in all youx actions ; doing everyone of them to the uttermost of your power, as our Lord Himself would have done them.

entries.chapterTitle: Every satisfaction offered to the senses which is not for God's honour
entries.textEn: Every satisfaction offered to the senses which is not for God's honour and glory you must renounce and reject for the love of Jesus Christ, Who, while upon earth, had, and sought for, no other pleasure than doing the will of His Father ; this, He said, was His meat and drink.

entries.chapterTitle: In none of your actions whatever should you take any man, however holy
entries.textEn: In none of your actions whatever should you take any man, however holy he may be, for your example, because Satan is sure to put his imperfections forward so as to attract your attention. Rather imitate Jesus Christ, Who is supremely perfect and supremely holy. So doing you will never fall into error.

entries.chapterTitle: Inwardly and outwardly live always crucified with Christ, and you will
entries.textEn: Inwardly and outwardly live always crucified with Christ, and you will attain unto peace and contentment of spirit, and in your patience you shall possess your soul.

entries.chapterTitle: Let Christ crucified alone be enough for you ;
entries.textEn: Let Christ crucified alone be enough for you ; with Him suffer, with Him take your rest, never rest nor suffer without Him ; striving with all your might to rid yourself of all selfish affections and inclinations in the annihilation of self.

entries.chapterTitle: He who makes any account whatever of himself, neither denies himself
entries.textEn: He who makes any account whatever of himself, neither denies himself nor follows Christ.

entries.chapterTitle: Love tribulations more than all good things, and do not imagine that
entries.textEn: Love tribulations more than all good things, and do not imagine that you are doing anything when you endure them ; so shall you please Him who did not hesitate to die for you.

entries.chapterTitle: If you wish to attain to the possession of Christ, never seek Him
entries.textEn: If you wish to attain to the possession of Christ, never seek Him without the Cross.

entries.chapterTitle: He who seeks not the Cross of Christ, seeks not the glory of Christ
entries.textEn: He who seeks not the Cross of Christ, seeks not the glory of Christ.

entries.chapterTitle: Desire to make yourself in suffering somewhat like our great God,
entries.textEn: Desire to make yourself in suffering somewhat like our great God, humiliated and crucified ; for life, if not an imitation of Him, is worth nothing.

entries.chapterTitle: What does he know who does not know how to suffer for Christ ?
entries.textEn: What does he know who does not know how to suffer for Christ ? The greater and the heavier the sufferings -- when suffering is in question -- the better is his lot who suffers.

entries.chapterTitle: All men desire to enter into the treasures and consolations of God ;
entries.textEn: All men desire to enter into the treasures and consolations of God ; but few desire to enter into tribulations and sorrows for the Son of God.

entries.chapterTitle: Jesus Christ is but little known of those who consider themselves His friends;
entries.textEn: Jesus Christ is but little known of those who consider themselves His friends; for we see them seeking in Him their own comfort, and not His bitter sorrows.

entries.chapterTitle: Because it is the function of the theological virtues to withdraw the
entries.textEn: Because it is the function of the theological virtues to withdraw the soul from all that is less than God, it is theirs also to unite it with Him.

entries.chapterTitle: Without walking truly in the practice of these three virtues, it is
entries.textEn: Without walking truly in the practice of these three virtues, it is impossible to attain to the perfect love of God. FAITH.

entries.chapterTitle: The way of Faith is sound and safe, and along this souls must journey
entries.textEn: The way of Faith is sound and safe, and along this souls must journey on from virtue to virtue, shutting their eyes against every object of sense and of clear and particular perception.

entries.chapterTitle: When the inspirations are from God they are always in the order of the
entries.textEn: When the inspirations are from God they are always in the order of the motives of His Law, and of the Faith, in the perfection of which the soul should ever draw nearer and nearer on the way to God.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that travels in the light and verities of the Faith is secured
entries.textEn: The soul that travels in the light and verities of the Faith is secured against error, for error proceeds ordinarily from our own proper desires, tastes, reflections, and understanding, wherein there is generally too much or too little ; and hence the inclination to that which is not seemly.

entries.chapterTitle: By Faith the soul travels protected against the devil, its strongest
entries.textEn: By Faith the soul travels protected against the devil, its strongest and craftiest foe ; and S. Peter knew of no stronger defence against him when he said : Resist him, strong in faith.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that would draw near unto God and unite itself with Him, must
entries.textEn: The soul that would draw near unto God and unite itself with Him, must do so by not comprehending rather than by comprehending, in utter forgetfulness of created things ; because it must exchange the mutable and comprehensible for the immutable and the incomprehensible, Who is God.

entries.chapterTitle: Outward light enables us to see that we may not fall ;
entries.textEn: Outward light enables us to see that we may not fall ; it is otherwise in the things of God, for there it is better not to see, and the soul, not seeing, is in greater security.

entries.chapterTitle: It being certain that in this life we know God better by what He is not
entries.textEn: It being certain that in this life we know God better by what He is not than by what He is, it is necessary, if we are to draw near unto Him, that the soul must deny, to the uttermost, all that may be denied of its apprehensions, both natural and supernatural.

entries.chapterTitle: All apprehension and knowledge of supernatural things cannot help us to
entries.textEn: All apprehension and knowledge of supernatural things cannot help us to love God so much as the least act of living Faith and Hope made in detachment from all things.

entries.chapterTitle: As in natural generation no new form results without the corruption of
entries.textEn: As in natural generation no new form results without the corruption of the one previously existing -- for this obstructs the former by reason of the contrariety between them -- so, while the soul is under the dominion of the sensual and animal spirit, the pure and heavenly spirit can never enter within it.

entries.chapterTitle: Let no created thing have a place in your heart if you would have the
entries.textEn: Let no created thing have a place in your heart if you would have the face of God pure and clear in your soul ; yea, rather empty your spirit of all created things, and you will walk in the Divine light ; for God resembles no created thing.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul is most recollected in Faith ;
entries.textEn: The soul is most recollected in Faith ; for then the Holy Ghost gives it light: the more pure and refined the soul in a perfect living Faith, the greater the infusion of Charity, and the greater the communication of supernatural gifts and light.

entries.chapterTitle: One of the greatest gifts of God to the soul in this life not permanent
entries.textEn: One of the greatest gifts of God to the soul in this life not permanent but transient -- is that deep sense and understanding of God by which it feels and understands clearly, that it can neither understand nor feel Him at all.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that leans upon any understanding, sense, or feeling of its
entries.textEn: The soul that leans upon any understanding, sense, or feeling of its own -- all this being very little and very unlike to God -- in order to travel on the right road, is most easily led astray or impeded, because it is not perfectly blind in Faith, which is its true guide.

entries.chapterTitle: There is one thing in our day that ought to make us afraid : persons
entries.textEn: There is one thing in our day that ought to make us afraid : persons who have hardly begun to make their meditations, if they seem to hear anything during their recollection, pronounce it to have come from God ; so they tell us, God has spoken or I have had an answer from God. In truth all this is nothing: these persons have been speaking to themselves, out of a longing for such communications.

entries.chapterTitle: He who should now enquire of God by vision or revelation would offend
entries.textEn: He who should now enquire of God by vision or revelation would offend Him, because he does not fix his eyes upon Christ alone. To such an one the answer of God is : This is my beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased, hear Him, and do not seek for new instructions, for in Him I have spoken and revealed all that can be asked or desired, and I have given Him to be your Brother, Master, Companion, Ransom, and Reward.

entries.chapterTitle: We must be guided in all things by the teaching of Christ and His
entries.textEn: We must be guided in all things by the teaching of Christ and His Church, and thereby seek the remedy for our spiritual ignorances and infirmities : it is thus that we shall obtain abundant relief ; and all that goes beyond this is not only curiosity but great rashness.

entries.chapterTitle: You are not to believe that which reaches you in a supernatural way,
entries.textEn: You are not to believe that which reaches you in a supernatural way, but only that which reaches you through the teaching of Christ and His ministers.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that seeks after revelations sins venially at least;
entries.textEn: The soul that seeks after revelations sins venially at least; so does the director who encourages or allows that seeking, be the end sought never so good : there is no necessity for this, seeing that we have our natural reason and the Evangelical Law to guide us in all things.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that desires revelations undermines the perfect guidance of
entries.textEn: The soul that desires revelations undermines the perfect guidance of the Faith, and opens a door for Satan to deceive it by false revelations; for he knows well how to disguise them so as to make them appear good.

entries.chapterTitle: The wisdom of the Saints consists in knowing how to direct the will
entries.textEn: The wisdom of the Saints consists in knowing how to direct the will courageously to God, in the perfect fulfilment of His law and His holy counsels. HOPE.

entries.chapterTitle: That which moves and overcomes God is earnest Hope ;
entries.textEn: That which moves and overcomes God is earnest Hope ; in order to attain to the union of love, the soul must journey in hope of God alone ; for without it nothing will be obtained.

entries.chapterTitle: A living Hope in God gives the soul such courage and elevation in the
entries.textEn: A living Hope in God gives the soul such courage and elevation in the things of everlasting life, that it looks on this world -- so indeed it is -- as dry, weak, valueless, and dead, in comparison with that it hopes for hereafter.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul in Hope strips itself of all the trappings of this world,
entries.textEn: The soul in Hope strips itself of all the trappings of this world, setting the heart upon nothing, hoping for nothing in it or of it, clad in the vesture of hope of everlasting life.

entries.chapterTitle: Through a living Hope in God the heart is so raised up above the world
entries.textEn: Through a living Hope in God the heart is so raised up above the world and delivered from all its snares, that it can neither be touched nor even be seen by it.

entries.chapterTitle: In all your trials have recourse to God in all confidence, and you will
entries.textEn: In all your trials have recourse to God in all confidence, and you will be comforted, enlightened, and instructed.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that retains the slightest desire for earthly things, is more
entries.textEn: The soul that retains the slightest desire for earthly things, is more unseemly and impure in the way of God than if it were labouring under the heaviest and most impure temptations, provided the natural will did not consent to them ; such a soul may, with greater confidence, draw near to God in obedience to the Divine will ; for our Lord hath said: Come unto me all you who labour and are heavily burdened, and I will refresh you.

entries.chapterTitle: Have an interior desire that God may give you all He knows to be
entries.textEn: Have an interior desire that God may give you all He knows to be needful for you, to His greater honour and glory.

entries.chapterTitle: Have a continual trust in God, esteeming in yourself and in your
entries.textEn: Have a continual trust in God, esteeming in yourself and in your brethren that which He most esteems ; namely, spiritual good.

entries.chapterTitle: The more God gives, the more He makes us desire;
entries.textEn: The more God gives, the more He makes us desire; until He leaves us empty that He may fill us with His blessings.

entries.chapterTitle: So pleased is God with the soul hoping in Him, and looking to nothing
entries.textEn: So pleased is God with the soul hoping in Him, and looking to nothing else, that it may be truly said the more that soul hopes for, the more it obtains.

entries.chapterTitle: If you have sweetness and delight, draw near to God in fear and in
entries.textEn: If you have sweetness and delight, draw near to God in fear and in truth, and you will never be deceived nor entangled in vanity.

entries.chapterTitle: Do not rejoice in temporal prosperity, because you do not certainly
entries.textEn: Do not rejoice in temporal prosperity, because you do not certainly know that your eternal life is secure.

entries.chapterTitle: Though a man prosper in all his undertakings, and though every wish of
entries.textEn: Though a man prosper in all his undertakings, and though every wish of his heart may be gratified, he ought in such a case to fear rather than rejoice ; for this multiplies the occasions of forgetting God, and the risks of offending Him.

entries.chapterTitle: Do not presume upon vain joy ;
entries.textEn: Do not presume upon vain joy ; knowing how many and how grievous are the sins you have committed, and not knowing whether you are pleasing unto God. But always fear and always hope in God.

entries.chapterTitle: How can you venture to live without fear, seeing that you must appear
entries.textEn: How can you venture to live without fear, seeing that you must appear before God to give account of your lightest words and thoughts ?

entries.chapterTitle: Lo ! many are called and few are chosen ;
entries.textEn: Lo ! many are called and few are chosen ; and if you are not careful, your final ruin is more certain than your salvation ; for the way that leadeth to eternal life is strait.

entries.chapterTitle: As in the hour of death you will certainly be sorry that you have not
entries.textEn: As in the hour of death you will certainly be sorry that you have not employed all your time in the service of God, why is it that you do not now so employ your time, as you will wish you had done when you shall come to die? CHARITY.

entries.chapterTitle: The strength of the soul lies in its faculties, passions, and desires ;
entries.textEn: The strength of the soul lies in its faculties, passions, and desires ; if these be directed towards God by the will, and withdrawn from all that is not God, the soul then keeps its strength for Him and loves Him with all its might, as our Lord commands us.

entries.chapterTitle: Charity is like a fine robe of many colours, which lends grace, beauty,
entries.textEn: Charity is like a fine robe of many colours, which lends grace, beauty, and freshness, not only to the white garment of Faith and the green vesture of Hope, but also to all the virtues; for without Charity no virtue is pleasing in the sight of God.

entries.chapterTitle: The worth of love does not consist in high feelings, but in detachment
entries.textEn: The worth of love does not consist in high feelings, but in detachment : in patience under trials for the sake of God Whom we love.

entries.chapterTitle: God has a greater esteem for the lowest degree of purity of conscience,
entries.textEn: God has a greater esteem for the lowest degree of purity of conscience, than for the greatest service you can render Him if that be wanting.

entries.chapterTitle: To seek God for Himself is to be without every consolation for His sake
entries.textEn: To seek God for Himself is to be without every consolation for His sake : an inclination to the choice of all that is most unpleasing, whether in the things of God or in the things of the world ; this is to love God.

entries.chapterTitle: Do not imagine that God is pleased with many good works, so much as
entries.textEn: Do not imagine that God is pleased with many good works, so much as with the doing of them with a good will, without self-seeking or human respect.

entries.chapterTitle: Herein a man may know whether he really loves God : Is he satisfied
entries.textEn: Herein a man may know whether he really loves God : Is he satisfied with anything less than God ?

entries.chapterTitle: As the hair which is frequently dressed is the cleaner, and is the more
entries.textEn: As the hair which is frequently dressed is the cleaner, and is the more easily dressed upon all occasions, so is it with the soul which frequently examines its thoughts, words, and works, doing all things for the love of God.

entries.chapterTitle: As the hair is to be dressed from the top of the head if it is to be
entries.textEn: As the hair is to be dressed from the top of the head if it is to be thoroughly cleansed, so our good works must have their beginning in the height of the love of God, if they are to be thoroughly pure and clean.

entries.chapterTitle: To restrain the tongue and the thoughts, and to set the affections
entries.textEn: To restrain the tongue and the thoughts, and to set the affections regularly upon God, quickly sets the soul on fire in a Divine way.

entries.chapterTitle: Study always to please God;
entries.textEn: Study always to please God; pray that His will may be accomplished in you; love Him much, for it is His due.

entries.chapterTitle: All our goodness is a loan ;
entries.textEn: All our goodness is a loan ; God is the owner ; God worketh, and His work is God.

entries.chapterTitle: We gain more by the goods of God in one hour, than in our whole life by our own
entries.textEn: We gain more by the goods of God in one hour, than in our whole life by our own.

entries.chapterTitle: Our Lord has always manifested the treasures of His wisdom and His
entries.textEn: Our Lord has always manifested the treasures of His wisdom and His Spirit to men : but now that wickedness manifests itself the more, He manifests them still more.

entries.chapterTitle: In one sense the purification of a soul from the contradictions of
entries.textEn: In one sense the purification of a soul from the contradictions of desire is a greater work of God than its creation out of nothing ; that nothing offered no resistance to His Majesty : not so the desires of the creature.

entries.chapterTitle: That which God intends is to make us God by participation, He being God
entries.textEn: That which God intends is to make us God by participation, He being God by nature ; as the fire changes everything into fire.

entries.chapterTitle: At the close of life you will be examined as to your love : learn then
entries.textEn: At the close of life you will be examined as to your love : learn then to love God as He wishes to be loved, and give up all that is your own.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that seeks God wholly, must give itself wholly to Him
entries.textEn: The soul that seeks God wholly, must give itself wholly to Him.

entries.chapterTitle: New and imperfect lovers are like new wine, easily spoiled until the
entries.textEn: New and imperfect lovers are like new wine, easily spoiled until the sum of imperfections has been cleared away, and the heat with gross satisfaction of the senses has died out.

entries.chapterTitle: The passions rule over the soul and assail it in proportion to the
entries.textEn: The passions rule over the soul and assail it in proportion to the weakness of the will in God, and to its dependence on creatures ; for then it rejoices so easily in things which do not deserve to be rejoiced in; hopes for that which is of no profit, and grieves over that in which perhaps it ought to rejoice, and fears where there is nothing to be afraid of.

entries.chapterTitle: They provoke the Divine Majesty to anger exceedingly, who, seeking for
entries.textEn: They provoke the Divine Majesty to anger exceedingly, who, seeking for spiritual food, are not content with God only, but intermingle therewith carnal and earthly satisfactions.

entries.chapterTitle: He who loves any other thing with God makes light of Him, because He
entries.textEn: He who loves any other thing with God makes light of Him, because He puts into the balance with Him that which is at an infinite distance from Him.

entries.chapterTitle: As a sick man is too weak for work, so the soul that is weak in the
entries.textEn: As a sick man is too weak for work, so the soul that is weak in the love of God is also too weak for the practice of perfect virtue.

entries.chapterTitle: To seek self in God is to seek for comfort and refreshment from God;
entries.textEn: To seek self in God is to seek for comfort and refreshment from God; now this is contrary to the pure love of God.

entries.chapterTitle: To regard the gifts of God more than God Himself, is a great evil
entries.textEn: To regard the gifts of God more than God Himself, is a great evil.

entries.chapterTitle: Many there are who seek their own pleasure and comfort in God, and on
entries.textEn: Many there are who seek their own pleasure and comfort in God, and on whom He bestows His gifts and graces ; but they who seek to please Him and to give Him something at their own cost -- setting their own pleasure aside are very few.

entries.chapterTitle: Few spiritual persons -- even among those who think themselves most
entries.textEn: Few spiritual persons -- even among those who think themselves most advanced -- attain to a perfect resolution in well-doing, for they never entirely lose themselves on some point or other connected with the world or self, despising appearances and the opinions of men, so as to make their good works perfect and in detachment from all things for the sake of Christ.

entries.chapterTitle: Self-will and self-satisfaction in the works they do so prevail among
entries.textEn: Self-will and self-satisfaction in the works they do so prevail among men, whether ordinary or more advanced Christians, that scarcely one is to be found who works simply for God without looking for some consolation or comfort or other advantage in his work.

entries.chapterTitle: Some souls call God their Spouse and their Beloved ;
entries.textEn: Some souls call God their Spouse and their Beloved ; but He is not really beloved by them, because their heart is not whole with Him.

entries.chapterTitle: What good will it do you if you give God one thing when He asks something else ?
entries.textEn: What good will it do you if you give God one thing when He asks something else ? Consider what God wills, and do it, for so will you satisfy your heart better than by doing that to which you are inclined yourself.

entries.chapterTitle: To find all satisfaction in God you must be satisfied with Him only,
entries.textEn: To find all satisfaction in God you must be satisfied with Him only, for in heaven itself, if you did not bend your will to His will, you would never be satisfied ; so is it here, if your heart is set upon anything other than God.

entries.chapterTitle: As aromatic spices exposed to the air gradually lose their fragrance
entries.textEn: As aromatic spices exposed to the air gradually lose their fragrance and the strength of their perfume, so the soul, not recollected in the love of God alone, loses the heat and vigour of virtue.

entries.chapterTitle: He who seeks nothing but God walks not in darkness, however blind and
entries.textEn: He who seeks nothing but God walks not in darkness, however blind and poor he may be in his own estimation.

entries.chapterTitle: For a man to be in pain for God is a sign that he has given himself up
entries.textEn: For a man to be in pain for God is a sign that he has given himself up to Him, and that he loves Him.

entries.chapterTitle: He who in the midst of dryness and abandonment is painfully anxious
entries.textEn: He who in the midst of dryness and abandonment is painfully anxious about God, and afraid that he does not serve Him, offers Him a sacrifice that pleaseth Him well.

entries.chapterTitle: When God is really loved, He hears most readily the cry of the sdul
entries.textEn: When God is really loved, He hears most readily the cry of the sdul that loves Him.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul defends itself against its fleshly enemy by charity ;
entries.textEn: The soul defends itself against its fleshly enemy by charity ; for where there is a real love of God neither the love of self nor the love of creatures can enter in.

entries.chapterTitle: The loving soul is meek, gentle, humble, and patient;
entries.textEn: The loving soul is meek, gentle, humble, and patient; the soul that is hard in self-love hardens itself still more. If Thou, 0 good Jesus, in Thy love dost not make the soul gentle, it will persist in its natural hardness.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that loves is neither wearied nor wearies
entries.textEn: The soul that loves is neither wearied nor wearies.

entries.chapterTitle: Behold the infinite wisdom and the hidden mysteries ;
entries.textEn: Behold the infinite wisdom and the hidden mysteries ; the peace, the love, the silence of the Divine Bosom ; the deep science God teaches there ; what we call anagogic acts -- ejaculatory prayer -- how they set the heart on fire!

entries.chapterTitle: The perfect love of God cannot subsist without the knowledge of God and of self
entries.textEn: The perfect love of God cannot subsist without the knowledge of God and of self.

entries.chapterTitle: Perfect love naturally seeks nothing, and claims nothing, for itself,
entries.textEn: Perfect love naturally seeks nothing, and claims nothing, for itself, but all for the beloved ; if this be the case with earthly love, how much more with the love of God?

entries.chapterTitle: The ancient friends of God scarcely ever fail Him, because they are
entries.textEn: The ancient friends of God scarcely ever fail Him, because they are raised above all occasions of failure.

entries.chapterTitle: True love accepts prosperity and adversity with an equal spirit, that
entries.textEn: True love accepts prosperity and adversity with an equal spirit, that of joy and delight.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that labours to divest itself of all that is not God for God's
entries.textEn: The soul that labours to divest itself of all that is not God for God's sake is immediately enlightened by, and transformed in, God, in such a way that the soul seems to be God Himself, and to possess the things of God.

entries.chapterTitle: Satan fears a soul united with God, as he fears God Himself
entries.textEn: Satan fears a soul united with God, as he fears God Himself.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul, in the union of love, resists even the first impulses
entries.textEn: The soul, in the union of love, resists even the first impulses.

entries.chapterTitle: Purity of heart is nothing less than the love and grace of God
entries.textEn: Purity of heart is nothing less than the love and grace of God. Hence our Lord says : Blessed are the pure in heart ; that is, those who love ; for blessedness is given to nothing less than love.

entries.chapterTitle: He who truly loves God does not blush before men for what he does for God ;
entries.textEn: He who truly loves God does not blush before men for what he does for God ; neither does he conceal his good works out of shame, though the whole world may condemn them.

entries.chapterTitle: He who truly Joves God thinks it a great gain to lose all he has, and
entries.textEn: He who truly Joves God thinks it a great gain to lose all he has, and his own life, for God.

entries.chapterTitle: If the soul had but one glimpse of the beauty of God, not only would it
entries.textEn: If the soul had but one glimpse of the beauty of God, not only would it desire to die that it might see Him for ever, but it would joyfully undergo a thousand most bitter deaths to see Him again, if only for a moment.

entries.chapterTitle: He who acts out of the pure love of God, not only * does not perform
entries.textEn: He who acts out of the pure love of God, not only * does not perform his actions to be seen of men, but does not do them even that God may know of them. Such an one, if he thought it possible that his good works might escape the eye of God, would still perform them with the same joy, and in the same pureness of love.

entries.chapterTitle: It is a great matter to be much exercised in love: in order that the
entries.textEn: It is a great matter to be much exercised in love: in order that the soul, made perfect and consummated therein, may not be long detained, either in this life or the next, from the vision of God.

entries.chapterTitle: A pure and perfect work, wrought for God in a pure heart, makes a
entries.textEn: A pure and perfect work, wrought for God in a pure heart, makes a perfect kingdom for its Lord.

entries.chapterTitle: To the pure in heart high things and low are profitable
entries.textEn: To the pure in heart high things and low are profitable. and minister to their greater purity ; while to the impure, by reason of their impurity, both the one and the other are occasions of greater evil.

entries.chapterTitle: The pure in heart find in all things the knowledge of God, sweet,
entries.textEn: The pure in heart find in all things the knowledge of God, sweet, chaste, pure, spiritual, joyous, and loving. PEACE.

entries.chapterTitle: By keeping guard over the senses, which are the gates of the soul, we
entries.textEn: By keeping guard over the senses, which are the gates of the soul, we keep also and increase its tranquillity and purity.

entries.chapterTitle: Man would never lose peace if he forgot and cast aside his thoughts and
entries.textEn: Man would never lose peace if he forgot and cast aside his thoughts and notions, and withdrew from the sight, hearing, and discussion of passing events, so far as he well may.

entries.chapterTitle: If we forget all created things, there is then nothing to disturb our peace ;
entries.textEn: If we forget all created things, there is then nothing to disturb our peace ; nothing to excite our desires. These are they that disturb it ; for, as the proverb says, What the eye hath not seen, the heart does not desire.

entries.chapterTitle: The restless and perturbed soul, not built up in mortification of the
entries.textEn: The restless and perturbed soul, not built up in mortification of the passions and desires, is, as such, incapacitated for spiritual good, for that enters only into the soul which is under control and ordered in peace.

entries.chapterTitle: God reigns only in the peaceful and unselfish soul
entries.textEn: God reigns only in the peaceful and unselfish soul.

entries.chapterTitle: Be tranquil;
entries.textEn: Be tranquil; put away superfluous thoughts, and make light of whatever may happen ; so shall your service be pleasing unto God, and you shall rejoice in Him.

entries.chapterTitle: Keep your heart in peace ;
entries.textEn: Keep your heart in peace ; let nothing in this world disturb it : all things have an end.

entries.chapterTitle: Be not made sad by the adverse events of this life, for you know not
entries.textEn: Be not made sad by the adverse events of this life, for you know not the good they bring with them, ordained in the justice of God, for the everlasting joy of the elect.

entries.chapterTitle: In all circumstances, however hard they may be, we should rejoice,
entries.textEn: In all circumstances, however hard they may be, we should rejoice, rather than be cast down, that we may not lose the greatest good, the peace and tranquillity of our soul.

entries.chapterTitle: If the whole world and all that is in it were thrown into confusion,
entries.textEn: If the whole world and all that is in it were thrown into confusion, disquietude on that account would be vanity, because that disquietude would do more harm than good.

entries.chapterTitle: To .endure all things with an equable and peaceful mind, not only
entries.textEn: To .endure all things with an equable and peaceful mind, not only brings with it many blessings to the soul, but it also enables us, in the midst of our difficulties, to have a clear judgment about them, and to minister the fitting remedy for them.

entries.chapterTitle: It is not the will of God that the soul should be troubled by anything,
entries.textEn: It is not the will of God that the soul should be troubled by anything, or that it should be afflicted ; for if men are afflicted because of the adversities of this world, that is the effect of their being weak in virtue ; for the soul of the perfect rejoices even in that which gives pain to the soul of the imperfect.

entries.chapterTitle: The heavens are stedfast, not subject to generation ;
entries.textEn: The heavens are stedfast, not subject to generation ; and souls which are of a heavenly nature are stedfast, not subject to the generation of desires, nor of anything of that kind : they are in some measure like unto God, Who is not moved for ever.

entries.chapterTitle: Wisdom enters by love, silence, and mortification
entries.textEn: Wisdom enters by love, silence, and mortification. It is a great wisdom to know when to be silent, when to suffer, and never to regard the sayings, doings, or lives of others.

entries.chapterTitle: See that you do not intermeddle in the affairs of other people, nor
entries.textEn: See that you do not intermeddle in the affairs of other people, nor discuss them in your own thoughts; for perhaps you will not be able to fulfil your own task.

entries.chapterTitle: Do not entertain a suspicious thought of a brother, for that takes away
entries.textEn: Do not entertain a suspicious thought of a brother, for that takes away purity of heart.

entries.chapterTitle: Never listen to accounts of the frailties of others;
entries.textEn: Never listen to accounts of the frailties of others; and if anyone should complain to you of another, humbly ask him not to speak about him at all.

entries.chapterTitle: Do not shrink from trouble : though it may seem to you more than you can bear
entries.textEn: Do not shrink from trouble : though it may seem to you more than you can bear. Let all men find you compassionate.

entries.chapterTitle: No one merits love except for the virtue that he has ;
entries.textEn: No one merits love except for the virtue that he has ; and when love is so ordered, it is according to God and in. great freedom.

entries.chapterTitle: When the love and affection we give to the creature is purely spiritual
entries.textEn: When the love and affection we give to the creature is purely spiritual and founded on God, the love of God grows with it ; and the more we remember the earthly love, the more we also remember God and desire Him : the one grows apace with the other.

entries.chapterTitle: When the love of the creature springs from sensual vice, or from a
entries.textEn: When the love of the creature springs from sensual vice, or from a purely natural inclination, in proportion to its growth is the diminution of the love of God and forgetfulness of Him ; remorse of conscience comes from the recollection of the creature.

entries.chapterTitle: That which is bom of the flesh is flesh, and that which is bora of the
entries.textEn: That which is bom of the flesh is flesh, and that which is bora of the spirit is spirit, saith our Saviour in His Gospel. So the love which grows out of sensuality ends in sensuality ; that which is of the spirit ends in the Spirit of God, and makes it grow. This is the difference between these two loves, that men may distinguish between them.

entries.chapterTitle: He who loves any creature out of the order of charity becomes vile as
entries.textEn: He who loves any creature out of the order of charity becomes vile as that creature itself, and in one sense even viler ; for love not only levels but subjects also the lover to the object of his love.

entries.chapterTitle: The passions and desires, when under control and restrained, are the
entries.textEn: The passions and desires, when under control and restrained, are the sources of all virtues, and, when they have broken loose, of all the vices and imperfections of the soul also.

entries.chapterTitle: Every desire hurts the soul in five ways, beside robbing it of the
entries.textEn: Every desire hurts the soul in five ways, beside robbing it of the Spirit of God : 1. It fatigues it. it. 3. Obscures it. 4. Defiles it. 5. Weakens it.

entries.chapterTitle: All created things are but the crumbs which fall from the table of God ;
entries.textEn: All created things are but the crumbs which fall from the table of God ; and for that reason, they who go about feeding on the creature are rightly called dogs; they are, therefore, always hungry like dogs, and justly so, because crumbs excite, rather than appease, hunger.

entries.chapterTitle: The desires are like restless and dissatisfied children begging of
entries.textEn: The desires are like restless and dissatisfied children begging of their mother, now one thing, now another, never contented; like one ill of a burning fever, never at rest, and whose thirst increases while the fever lasts.

entries.chapterTitle: As a man dragging a cart up hill, so is that soul on its way to God,
entries.textEn: As a man dragging a cart up hill, so is that soul on its way to God, which does not throw aside the cares of this life, and which does not deny itself.

entries.chapterTitle: As he is tormented who falls into the hands of his enemies, so is the
entries.textEn: As he is tormented who falls into the hands of his enemies, so is the soul afflicted and tormented which is carried away by its desires.

entries.chapterTitle: As a man is tormented and afflicted who lies down naked amid thorns and
entries.textEn: As a man is tormented and afflicted who lies down naked amid thorns and briers, so is the soul tormented and afflicted which lies down in the midst of its desires: they pierce, torture, and tear it painfully.

entries.chapterTitle: As vapours obscure the air and hide the light of the sun, so the soul,
entries.textEn: As vapours obscure the air and hide the light of the sun, so the soul, captive to its desires, is intellectually in darkness, so that neither the sun of natural reason nor that of the supernatural wisdom of God can inform or enlighten it.

entries.chapterTitle: He who feeds his desires is like a moth, or a fish dazzled by the light
entries.textEn: He who feeds his desires is like a moth, or a fish dazzled by the light which the fishermen throw over the water, that it may not see the ruin which the fishermen have prepared for it.

entries.chapterTitle: Who can tell how impossible it is for the soul, subject to desires, to
entries.textEn: Who can tell how impossible it is for the soul, subject to desires, to judge of the things of God ? for while there is a film over the eye of its judgment, it sees nothing but that film, now of one colour, now of another ; and so it comes to regard the things of God as not the things of God, and those which are not the things of God as the things of God.

entries.chapterTitle: A bird that has perched upon a twig covered with birdlime labours in a
entries.textEn: A bird that has perched upon a twig covered with birdlime labours in a twofold way -- in extricating itself and in cleaning itself; so a soul, that has given way to desires ; it has to extricate itself in the first place, and then, when it has done so, it has to clean itself of that which has clung to it.

entries.chapterTitle: As soot defiles the most beautiful and perfect face, so the unruly
entries.textEn: As soot defiles the most beautiful and perfect face, so the unruly desires of the soul defile and pollute that soul which entertains them, and yet that soul in itself is the most beautiful and perfect image of God.

entries.chapterTitle: He that toucheth pitch, saith the Holy Ghost, shall be defiled with it
entries.textEn: He that toucheth pitch, saith the Holy Ghost, shall be defiled with it A soul touches pitch when it satisfies the desires of the will in any created thing.

entries.chapterTitle: If my object were to describe the foul and corrupt condition to which
entries.textEn: If my object were to describe the foul and corrupt condition to which the desires reduce the soul, I should not be able to find anything so full of cobwebs and worms, not even corruption itself, wherewith to compare it.

entries.chapterTitle: The desires are like the suckers which grow on a tree, they sap its
entries.textEn: The desires are like the suckers which grow on a tree, they sap its strength and destroy its fertility.

entries.chapterTitle: There are no corrupt humours which so enfeeble a man's gait, and make
entries.textEn: There are no corrupt humours which so enfeeble a man's gait, and make him to loathe his food, as the desire of the creature enfeebles the soul, indisposing it for the practice of virtue.

entries.chapterTitle: Many souls have no inclination for virtue, because their desires are
entries.textEn: Many souls have no inclination for virtue, because their desires are impure, and not for God.

entries.chapterTitle: As the young vipers, growing in the womb, feed on their mother and kill
entries.textEn: As the young vipers, growing in the womb, feed on their mother and kill her, preserving their own lives at the cost of hers, so the unmortified desires prey on the soul and kill the life of God in it ; they at last are the only things that live in it, because the soul has not killed them first.

entries.chapterTitle: As it is necessary to till the earth that it may bring forth fruit --
entries.textEn: As it is necessary to till the earth that it may bring forth fruit -- for otherwise it will produce nothing but weeds, so also is it necessary to mortify our desires, in order to have purity of soul.

entries.chapterTitle: As wood is never transformed into fire if but one degree of heat
entries.textEn: As wood is never transformed into fire if but one degree of heat necessary for that end be wanting, so the soul that has but one imperfection can never be perfectly transformed in God.

entries.chapterTitle: Whether it be a strong wire rope, or a slender and delicate thread,
entries.textEn: Whether it be a strong wire rope, or a slender and delicate thread, that holds the bird, it matters not if it really detains it, for, until the cord be broken, the bird cannot fly ; so the soul, held in the bonds of human affections, however slight they may be, cannot, while they last, fly upwards to God.

entries.chapterTitle: The desires and attachments of the soul have the property attributed to
entries.textEn: The desires and attachments of the soul have the property attributed to the remora, which, though it be but a little fish, yet it arrests the progress of the ship to which it clings.

entries.chapterTitle: O that spiritual men knew how they are losing the blessings and fulness
entries.textEn: O that spiritual men knew how they are losing the blessings and fulness of the Spirit, merely because they will not raise up their desires above trifles, and how they might have the sweetness of all things in the pure food of the Spirit of which the manna was a figure -- if they would only abstain from tasting other food.

entries.chapterTitle: The children of Israel did not find in the manna all the sweetness and
entries.textEn: The children of Israel did not find in the manna all the sweetness and strength they might have found in it ; not because the manna did not contain them, but because they longed for other meat.

entries.chapterTitle: Of one spark cometh a great fire, and one imperfection is enough to
entries.textEn: Of one spark cometh a great fire, and one imperfection is enough to beget another. We shall never see a soul negligent in resisting but one single desire, which has not many other desires, springing out of that weakness and imperfection from which the first proceeds.

entries.chapterTitle: Voluntary and perfectly deliberate desires, however slight they may be,
entries.textEn: Voluntary and perfectly deliberate desires, however slight they may be, if only habitual, are those which chiefly impede our progress to perfection.

entries.chapterTitle: Any imperfection to which the soul is attached is a greater injury to
entries.textEn: Any imperfection to which the soul is attached is a greater injury to virtue than a daily fall into many other and even greater imperfections, provided they do not result from the habitual indulgence of an evil inclination.

entries.chapterTitle: God is justly angry with those souls whom He, in the power of His arm,
entries.textEn: God is justly angry with those souls whom He, in the power of His arm, has delivered from the world, and from the occasions of grievous sins, but who are yet weak and negligent in mortifying certain imperfections; for this He permits them to fall in their desires from bad to worse.

entries.chapterTitle: Give heed to reason, that you may perform that which it dictates to you
entries.textEn: Give heed to reason, that you may perform that which it dictates to you in the way of God : and it will serve you more than all good works heedlessly done, and all the spiritual sweetness you aim at.

entries.chapterTitle: Blessed is he who, setting his own tastes and inclinations aside, looks
entries.textEn: Blessed is he who, setting his own tastes and inclinations aside, looks at things according to reason and justice, in order to accomplish them.

entries.chapterTitle: He who acts according to reason is as one who eats strong and substantial food ;
entries.textEn: He who acts according to reason is as one who eats strong and substantial food ; but he who in his works seeks the satisfaction of his own will, is as one who eats poor and unripe fruit.

entries.chapterTitle: No creature may transgress the limits which God has set for it in the
entries.textEn: No creature may transgress the limits which God has set for it in the order of its nature : and as He has appointed for man's governance certain natural and rational laws, the transgression thereof, by seeking for information in a supernatural way, is neither holy nor becoming : moreover, God is displeased ; and if at any time He vouchsafes an answer, it is out of condescension to the soul's weakness.

entries.chapterTitle: Man knows not how to order his joy and grief reasonably and prudently,
entries.textEn: Man knows not how to order his joy and grief reasonably and prudently, because he knows not the difference between good and evil.

entries.chapterTitle: We know not how to distinguish between our right hand and our left :
entries.textEn: We know not how to distinguish between our right hand and our left : for at every step we take evil for good and good for evil, and if this be as it were natural to us, what must it be if desire be added to our natural blindness ?

entries.chapterTitle: The desire, as desire, is blind, because in itself it regards not
entries.textEn: The desire, as desire, is blind, because in itself it regards not reason, which is that which ever guides and directs the soul aright in its operations : so the soul, whenever it is guided by its desires, is blind.

entries.chapterTitle: The angels are our shepherds, because they carry not only our message
entries.textEn: The angels are our shepherds, because they carry not only our message to God, but also those of God to our souls, feeding them with sweet inspirations and Divine communications : as good shepherds they protect us, and defend us from the wolves, which are the evil spirits.

entries.chapterTitle: Through the secret inspirations which the angels convey to the soul,
entries.textEn: Through the secret inspirations which the angels convey to the soul, they effect a deeper knowledge of God, and make it love Him the more, till they leave it wounded with love.

entries.chapterTitle: The Divine wisdom which in heaven illumines the angels, and cleanses
entries.textEn: The Divine wisdom which in heaven illumines the angels, and cleanses them of their ignorances, is the same which illumines men upon earth, and cleanses them of their errors and imperfections ; it flows from God through the first orders of the hierarchies down to the lowest, and thence to men.

entries.chapterTitle: The light of God, which illumines the angels, enlightening and setting
entries.textEn: The light of God, which illumines the angels, enlightening and setting them on fire with love, as pure spirits disposed for that inflowing, illumines men ordinarily in obscurity, pain, and distress, because of men's impurity and weakness : so is the sun to a weak eye ; the light it gives is painful.

entries.chapterTitle: When man has become spiritualised and refined in the fire of Divine
entries.textEn: When man has become spiritualised and refined in the fire of Divine love which purifies him, he then receives the union and inflowing of the loving illumination with the sweetness with which an angel receives them. There are souls who in this life receive a more perfect illumination than the angels.

entries.chapterTitle: When God gives great graces to a soul through the hands of an angel, He
entries.textEn: When God gives great graces to a soul through the hands of an angel, He ordinarily allows the devil to know it, that he may assail that soul with all his might, according to the measure of justice, in order that the victory may be the more prized, and the soul, faithful in temptation, maybe the more rewarded.

entries.chapterTitle: Remember that your guardian angel does not always move the will to act,
entries.textEn: Remember that your guardian angel does not always move the will to act, though he always enlightens the reason ; therefore do not promise yourself sensible sweetness always in your works, because reason and understanding are sufficient.

entries.chapterTitle: When the desires of man are occupied with anything that is not God they
entries.textEn: When the desires of man are occupied with anything that is not God they embarrass the soul and shut the door against the light by which the angel moves to virtue.

entries.chapterTitle: Consider what utter vanity it is to rejoice in anything but in the
entries.textEn: Consider what utter vanity it is to rejoice in anything but in the service of God, how dangerous and how fetal ; how ruinous it proved to the angels who rejoiced and had complacency in their own beauty and their natural endowments ! for this they fell foul into the abyss.

entries.chapterTitle: A soul without a director is like a kindled coal, which, if left by
entries.textEn: A soul without a director is like a kindled coal, which, if left by itself, cools instead of burning.

entries.chapterTitle: He who insists on being left to himself, without a director to guide
entries.textEn: He who insists on being left to himself, without a director to guide him, is like an unowned tree by the wayside ; however fruitful it may be, the travellers pick its fruit, and none of it ripens.

entries.chapterTitle: The tree that is cultivated and kept carefully by its owner produces
entries.textEn: The tree that is cultivated and kept carefully by its owner produces fruit in due season, and the owner is not disappointed.

entries.chapterTitle: He who falls alone remains alone in his fell;
entries.textEn: He who falls alone remains alone in his fell; he makes little account of his soul, because he trusts in himself alone.

entries.chapterTitle: He who is burdened when he falls, rises with difficulty under his burden
entries.textEn: He who is burdened when he falls, rises with difficulty under his burden.

entries.chapterTitle: He who falls, being blind, cannot rise, being blind and alone ;
entries.textEn: He who falls, being blind, cannot rise, being blind and alone ; and if he should rise by himself, he will walk in a direction that is not good for him.

entries.chapterTitle: If you are not afraid to fall by yourself, how can you venture to raise
entries.textEn: If you are not afraid to fall by yourself, how can you venture to raise yourself alone? Remember that two are better than one.

entries.chapterTitle: Our Lord did not say in His Gospel, where one is by himself there am I,
entries.textEn: Our Lord did not say in His Gospel, where one is by himself there am I, but where there are at the least two : this is to show us that no one should believe of himself, or confirm himself in the things which he thinks are those of God, without the counsel and direction of the Church and her ministers.

entries.chapterTitle: Woe to him that is alone, saith the Holy Ghost;
entries.textEn: Woe to him that is alone, saith the Holy Ghost; and therefore the soul has need of a director, for both will resist the devil more easily, being both together to learn and practise the truth.

entries.chapterTitle: It is the will of God that the government of one
entries.textEn: It is the will of God that the government of one . man should be in the hands of another, and that we should not give perfect credit to those matters which He communicates supernaturally Himself, until they shall have passed through the human channel of another man's mouth.

entries.chapterTitle: When God makes a particular revelation to a soul, he also inclines that
entries.textEn: When God makes a particular revelation to a soul, he also inclines that soul to make it known to the minister of His Church, who stands in His place.

entries.chapterTitle: It is not every one who is fitted for the direction of souls ;
entries.textEn: It is not every one who is fitted for the direction of souls ; it being a matter of the last importance to give right or wrong advice in so serious a matter as that.

entries.chapterTitle: Let the soul that would advance, and not go back, take care into whose
entries.textEn: Let the soul that would advance, and not go back, take care into whose hands it commits itself ; for, as is the master, so is the scholar, and as is the father so is the child.

entries.chapterTitle: The inclinations and tastes of the director are easily impressed upon
entries.textEn: The inclinations and tastes of the director are easily impressed upon the penitent.

entries.chapterTitle: The chief solicitude of spiritual directors should be to mortify every
entries.textEn: The chief solicitude of spiritual directors should be to mortify every desire of their penitents: to make them deny themselves in all they desire, so as to deliver them from so great misery.

entries.chapterTitle: However high the doctrine, adorned the eloquence, sublime the style,
entries.textEn: However high the doctrine, adorned the eloquence, sublime the style, the fruits of the sermon will be, in general, no better than the spirit of the preacher.

entries.chapterTitle: A good style and action, high doctrines and correct expression, have a
entries.textEn: A good style and action, high doctrines and correct expression, have a greater effect when accompanied by true spirituality ; but without that the will is scarcely or but little inflamed, though the senses may be charmed and the understanding delighted.

entries.chapterTitle: God is angry with those who teach His law and keep it not ;
entries.textEn: God is angry with those who teach His law and keep it not ; and who preach spirituality to others without being spiritual themselves.

entries.chapterTitle: For the highest parts, and even for the ordinary parts, of the way of
entries.textEn: For the highest parts, and even for the ordinary parts, of the way of perfection, you will scarcely find one capable guide throughout, such as men have need of : such an one must be wise, discreet, and experienced.

entries.chapterTitle: For though the foundations of direction be knowledge and discretion,
entries.textEn: For though the foundations of direction be knowledge and discretion, yet if directors be without experience, they will never be able to guide the soul in the way in which God is leading it ; they will make it go backwards, ordering it after low methods which they pick up in books.

entries.chapterTitle: He who shall presumptuously err in the direction of souls, being under
entries.textEn: He who shall presumptuously err in the direction of souls, being under obligation to give good counsel -- as everyone is in the office he undertakes -- shall not escape punishment according to the evil he has done; for the work of God -- and such is the direction of souls -- demands great caution and counsel.

entries.chapterTitle: Who can be like St
entries.textEn: Who can be like St. Paul, who was all things to all, that he might save all ? knowing all the ways by which God leads souls, which are so different one from another, that you can scarcely find one which in half its ways agrees with the ways of another.

entries.chapterTitle: The greatest honour we can render unto God, is to serve Him in
entries.textEn: The greatest honour we can render unto God, is to serve Him in evangelical perfection : and whatever is beside this is of no value or advantage to man.

entries.chapterTitle: One thought of man is of more value than the whole world ;
entries.textEn: One thought of man is of more value than the whole world ; God alone is, for that reason, the worthy object of it, and to Him alone is it due ; every thought of man, therefore, which is not given to God, is a robbery.

entries.chapterTitle: In all nature there are correspondences;
entries.textEn: In all nature there are correspondences; insensible things correspond with those that are insensible ; sense with things sensible ; and man's thoughts with the Spirit of God.

entries.chapterTitle: Never let your heart waste its affections, not even for a moment
entries.textEn: Never let your heart waste its affections, not even for a moment.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul cannot overcome the devil without prayer, nor penetrate his
entries.textEn: The soul cannot overcome the devil without prayer, nor penetrate his devices without humility and mortification ; for the weapons of God are prayer and the Cross of Christ.

entries.chapterTitle: In all our necessities, trials, and afflictions, there is no better nor
entries.textEn: In all our necessities, trials, and afflictions, there is no better nor safer remedy than prayer, and hope that God will provide -for us in His own way.

entries.chapterTitle: Let God be the spouse and friend of your soul, remain always in His
entries.textEn: Let God be the spouse and friend of your soul, remain always in His presence, and so you shall avoid sin, learn to love Him, and all things will prosper with you.

entries.chapterTitle: Enter into your innermost heart, and labour in the presence of God, the
entries.textEn: Enter into your innermost heart, and labour in the presence of God, the spouse of your soul, Who is ever present doing you good.

entries.chapterTitle: Strive to be continually in the presence of God, and to preserve the
entries.textEn: Strive to be continually in the presence of God, and to preserve the purity which He teaches.

entries.chapterTitle: By prayer aridity is expelled, devotion increased,' and the interior
entries.textEn: By prayer aridity is expelled, devotion increased,' and the interior practice of virtue established in the soul.

entries.chapterTitle: By shutting the eyes to the defects of others, keeping silence, and
entries.textEn: By shutting the eyes to the defects of others, keeping silence, and conversing continually with God, great imperfections are rooted out of the soul, which thereby becomes the mistress of great virtues.

entries.chapterTitle: When prayer is made in the pure and simple understanding of God, it
entries.textEn: When prayer is made in the pure and simple understanding of God, it seems to the soul to have lasted but a moment, though in fact it occupied much time : this is that prayer of a moment, of which it is said that it pierces the clouds.

entries.chapterTitle: The powers and senses of the soul should not be employed altogether
entries.textEn: The powers and senses of the soul should not be employed altogether upon anything unless it be a matter which cannot be neglected ; for the rest, they should be unoccupied for God.

entries.chapterTitle: Wait lovingly upon God, without any desire to feel or understand
entries.textEn: Wait lovingly upon God, without any desire to feel or understand anything particular in Him.

entries.chapterTitle: Strive to attain to that state in which nothing is of importance to
entries.textEn: Strive to attain to that state in which nothing is of importance to you, and you of importance to none, so that being utterly forgotten you may be with God in secret.

entries.chapterTitle: He who will not allow his desires to carry him away will wing his
entries.textEn: He who will not allow his desires to carry him away will wing his flight like a bird whose wings are strong.

entries.chapterTitle: Do not nourish your soul upon anything else but on God : repel the
entries.textEn: Do not nourish your soul upon anything else but on God : repel the remembrance of things, let peace and recollection fill your heart.

entries.chapterTitle: If you would attain to holy recollection, it must be by rejecting, and
entries.textEn: If you would attain to holy recollection, it must be by rejecting, and not by admitting.

entries.chapterTitle: Seek by reading and you will find by meditating;
entries.textEn: Seek by reading and you will find by meditating; cry in prayer and the door will be opened in contemplation.

entries.chapterTitle: True devotion and spirituality consist in perseverance in prayer, with
entries.textEn: True devotion and spirituality consist in perseverance in prayer, with patience and humility, distrusting yourself that you may please God only.

entries.chapterTitle: They call upon God in truth who pray for that which is most true : that
entries.textEn: They call upon God in truth who pray for that which is most true : that which belongs to their eternal salvation.

entries.chapterTitle: There is no better way to obtain the desires of our heart than to pray
entries.textEn: There is no better way to obtain the desires of our heart than to pray with all our might for that which is most pleasing unto God ; for then He will grant us not only our salvation but also that which He sees most expedient for us, though we may never ask for it, and though it may have never entered into our hearts to do so.

entries.chapterTitle: Let every soul understand that, although God may not succour it in its
entries.textEn: Let every soul understand that, although God may not succour it in its necessities when it cries. He will not however fail it when the time comes ; provided it does not lose heart and cease from prayer.

entries.chapterTitle: When the will, the moment it feels any joy in sensible things, rises
entries.textEn: When the will, the moment it feels any joy in sensible things, rises upwards in that joy to God, and when sensible things move it to pray, it ought not then to reject, yea rather it should make use of, them for so holy an exercise ; because sensible things, under these conditions, subserve the end for which God created them : namely, to be occasions of making Him better loved and known.

entries.chapterTitle: He whose senses are subject to the Spirit, purged from all sensible
entries.textEn: He whose senses are subject to the Spirit, purged from all sensible objects, even in his first movements, elicits delights in the sweet knowledge and contemplation of God.

entries.chapterTitle: As it is a truth of sound philosophy that the life of every creature is
entries.textEn: As it is a truth of sound philosophy that the life of every creature is in harmony with its constitution, so is it clear beyond all contradiction, that he whose life is spiritual the animal life being mortified -- must be wholly tending towards God.

entries.chapterTitle: The will of a devout person rests chiefly on the invisible ;
entries.textEn: The will of a devout person rests chiefly on the invisible ; he requires but few images for his use, and these are such as are more conformable to Divine, than to human, taste ; ordering himself herein after the ways of the other world, and not of this.

entries.chapterTitle: The chief thing to be regarded in images is devotion and faith ;
entries.textEn: The chief thing to be regarded in images is devotion and faith ; if these be absent, the image will not be sufficient.
