What a perfect living image our Lord was upon earth, and yet those who had no faith, though they were constantly about Him, and saw His wonderful works, were not the better for His presence.

entries.chapterTitle: Keep yourself apart for one thing only, which brings everything with it
entries.textEn: Keep yourself apart for one thing only, which brings everything with it -- solitude, accompanied by prayer and spiritual reading : and there abide, forgetting all things, if there be no obligation upon you to remember them. You will please God more by keeping watch over, and perfecting yourself, than if you gained everything : for what doth it profit a man if he gain the whole world, if he loses his own soul ?

entries.chapterTitle: Pure spirituality gives no heed to matters which do not concern it, nor
entries.textEn: Pure spirituality gives no heed to matters which do not concern it, nor to human respect ; but alone and apart from all created forms, communicates interiorly in sweet tranquillity with God ; for the knowledge of Him lies in the Divine silence.

entries.chapterTitle: For the purposes of prayer that place is to be chosen in which sense
entries.textEn: For the purposes of prayer that place is to be chosen in which sense and spirit may be least hindered from rising up to God.

entries.chapterTitle: The place of prayer must not be pleasant and delectable to the senses
entries.textEn: The place of prayer must not be pleasant and delectable to the senses -- some people seek such a place -- lest the issue should be recreation of the senses, and not recollection of spirit. He who goes on a pilgrimage will do well to do so when others do not, though it be at an unusual season. When pilgrims are many, I would advise staying at home, for in general men return more dissipated than they were before they went. And they who become pilgrims for recreation, rather than devotion, are many in number.

entries.chapterTitle: He who interrupts the course of his spiritual exercises and prayer, is
entries.textEn: He who interrupts the course of his spiritual exercises and prayer, is like a man who allows a bird to escape from his hand ; he can hardly catch it again.

entries.chapterTitle: God being, as He is, inaccessible, do not repose on the consideration
entries.textEn: God being, as He is, inaccessible, do not repose on the consideration of objects perceptible by sense, and comprehended by the understanding. This is to be satisfied with what is less than God ; so doing you will destroy that energy of the soul which is necessary for drawing near unto Him.

entries.chapterTitle: Never consent to admit into your soul that which is not substantially
entries.textEn: Never consent to admit into your soul that which is not substantially spiritual ; for if you do so you will lose the sweetness of devotion and recollection.

entries.chapterTitle: He who relies much on the senses will never be very spiritual ;
entries.textEn: He who relies much on the senses will never be very spiritual ; they deceive themselves who think they can, in the sheer strength of our grovelling senses, attain to the power of the spirit.

entries.chapterTitle: The imperfect destroy true devotion, because they seek sensible
entries.textEn: The imperfect destroy true devotion, because they seek sensible sweetness in prayer.

entries.chapterTitle: The fly that touches the honey cannot fly;
entries.textEn: The fly that touches the honey cannot fly; so the soul that clings to spiritual sweetness ruins its own freedom and hinders contemplation.

entries.chapterTitle: He who will not dispose himself to pray in every place, but only there
entries.textEn: He who will not dispose himself to pray in every place, but only there where his own taste is gratified, will frequently fail in his prayer ; because, as they say, he can pray only in his own parish.

entries.chapterTitle: He who does not feel liberty of spirit amid the things of sense and
entries.textEn: He who does not feel liberty of spirit amid the things of sense and sweetness, which should serve as motives to prayer, and whose will rests and feeds upon them, ought to abstain from the use of them, for to him they are a hindrance on the road to God.

entries.chapterTitle: It is very foolish, when spiritual sweetness and delight fail, to
entries.textEn: It is very foolish, when spiritual sweetness and delight fail, to imagine that God has failed us also ; and to imagine, that because we have such sweetness, that we have God also.

entries.chapterTitle: Very often many spiritual persons employ their senses upon sensible
entries.textEn: Very often many spiritual persons employ their senses upon sensible things, under the pretext of giving themselves to prayer, and raising their hearts to God ; now this that they do should be called recreation rather than prayer; pleasing themselves rather than God.

entries.chapterTitle: Meditation tends to contemplation, as means to an end
entries.textEn: Meditation tends to contemplation, as means to an end. So when the end is attained, the means are laid aside ; men rest at the end of their journey ; thus, when the state of contemplation has been attained, meditation must cease.

entries.chapterTitle: As it is necessary, at the proper time, to give up the work of
entries.textEn: As it is necessary, at the proper time, to give up the work of reflection and meditation in order to draw near unto God, lest it should prove an impediment, so also is it necessary not to give it up before the time lest we should go back.

entries.chapterTitle: There are three signs of contemplation and interior recollection of the soul : 1
entries.textEn: There are three signs of contemplation and interior recollection of the soul : 1. When the soul takes no pleasure in transitory things. 2. When it seeks solitude and silence, striving after that which is the more perfect. 3. When meditation, which was once a help, proves a hindrance. These three signs must be found together.

entries.chapterTitle: In the beginning of the state of contemplation the loving knowledge of
entries.textEn: In the beginning of the state of contemplation the loving knowledge of God is, as it were, imperceptible : in the first place, because it is most subtile and delicate, and, as it were, unfelt ; in the second place, because the soul has been accustomed to the practice of meditation, which is more cognisable by the senses.

entries.chapterTitle: The more the soul is disposed for tranquillity, the more will the
entries.textEn: The more the soul is disposed for tranquillity, the more will the loving knowledge of contemplation grow ; the soul will feel it and relish it more than all other things whatever ; because it brings with it peace and rest, sweetness and delight, without trouble.

entries.chapterTitle: They who have passed on to the state of contempla tion, must not for
entries.textEn: They who have passed on to the state of contempla tion, must not for that reason suppose that they are never to make their meditations any more ; for in the beginning the habit of it is not so established that they can have it whenever they will ; neither are they so far removed from meditation as to be unable to meditate as they were accustomed to do.

entries.chapterTitle: Except in the act of contemplation, in all exercises and good works,
entries.textEn: Except in the act of contemplation, in all exercises and good works, the soul must make use of good meditations on, and recollection of, what is good in such a way as to increase devotion and profit, particularly dwelling on the life, passion, and death of our Lord Jesus Christ, in order that its works, exercises, and life may be conformed to His.

entries.chapterTitle: The conditions of the 'solitary sparrow' are five: 1
entries.textEn: The conditions of the 'solitary sparrow' are five: 1. It ascends as high as it can. 2. It admits none to be its companion, even of its own kind. 3. It faces the wind. 4. It has no definite colour. 5. It sings sweetly. The contemplative soul must do the same ; it must rise high above transitory things, making no more account of them than if they never existed ; it must be so enamoured of solitude and silence as to suffer no creature to be in its company; it must face the wind of the Holy Ghost, corresponding to His inspirations, that so doing, it may become more worthy of His company; it must have no definite colour, bent upon nothing but on doing the will of God ; it must sing sweetly in contemplation and in the love of God.

entries.chapterTitle: Though occasionally, in the height of contemplation and pure intuition
entries.textEn: Though occasionally, in the height of contemplation and pure intuition of the Divinity, the soul may not remember the most sacred humanity of Christ, because God elevates the spirit to the most supernatural knowledge, yet studiously to forget it is in nowise seemly, seeing that by the contemplation thereof, and loving meditation thereon, the soul ascends to the highest state of union ; for Christ our Lord is the Truth, the Gate, the Way, and the Guide to all good.

entries.chapterTitle: The way of life demands little trouble and care, it demands denial of
entries.textEn: The way of life demands little trouble and care, it demands denial of the will rather than much knowledge ; he who inclines to pleasure and sweetness will be the less able to travel on it.

entries.chapterTitle: He who does not walk in the way of his own pleasure, nor in that of the
entries.textEn: He who does not walk in the way of his own pleasure, nor in that of the pleasures which come from God, nor in that of those which come from creatures, and never does his own will, he shall never stumble.

entries.chapterTitle: Though you may undertake great things, yet, if you will not learn to
entries.textEn: Though you may undertake great things, yet, if you will not learn to deny your own will and to be obedient, casting away all anxiety about yourself and your own affairs, you will make no progress in the way of perfection.

entries.chapterTitle: Let others teach you, let others order you, let others rule over you,
entries.textEn: Let others teach you, let others order you, let others rule over you, and you will become perfect.

entries.chapterTitle: God is more pleased with that soul which, in aridity and trouble of
entries.textEn: God is more pleased with that soul which, in aridity and trouble of spirit, is subject and obedient, than with that which, without obedience, performs all its duties with great sweetness of spirit.

entries.chapterTitle: God would rather have from you the lowest degree of obedience and
entries.textEn: God would rather have from you the lowest degree of obedience and subjection, than all those services you would render Him.

entries.chapterTitle: Subjection and obedience is the penance of reason and discretion ;
entries.textEn: Subjection and obedience is the penance of reason and discretion ; and is therefore a more pleasing sacrifice in the eyes of God than all other bodily penances.

entries.chapterTitle: Bodily penance, without obedience, is a most imperfect thing ;
entries.textEn: Bodily penance, without obedience, is a most imperfect thing ; beginners practise it out of a desire for it, and for the pleasure they find in it ; and therefore because they herein do their own will, they grow in vice, rather than in virtue.

entries.chapterTitle: Inasmuch as a double bitterness results from fulfilling one's own will,
entries.textEn: Inasmuch as a double bitterness results from fulfilling one's own will, do not fulfil it ; although it may be bitterness to remain quiet.

entries.chapterTitle: The devil prevails with ease over those who are alone, and who in the
entries.textEn: The devil prevails with ease over those who are alone, and who in the things of God order themselves according to their own will.

entries.chapterTitle: It is better when burdened to be joined to the strong, than unburdened
entries.textEn: It is better when burdened to be joined to the strong, than unburdened to the weak. When you are loaded with afflictions you are joined to God, Who is your strength, and He is the strength of the afflicted. When you are unburdened you are joined to yourself, who are weakness itself, for virtue and fortitude grow in the soul, and are strengthened, in tribulations.

entries.chapterTitle: Your flesh is weak, and no worldly thing can strengthen or comfort your spirit ;
entries.textEn: Your flesh is weak, and no worldly thing can strengthen or comfort your spirit ; that which is born of the world is worldly, and that which is born of the flesh is flesh : a good spirit is born only of the Spirit of God, and is communicated neither through the world nor the flesh.

entries.chapterTitle: The most delicate flower is the first to wither, and to lose its
entries.textEn: The most delicate flower is the first to wither, and to lose its fragrance : therefore take care you do not walk in the way of spiritual sweetness, for you will never be firm. Choose rather a strong spirit, attached to nothing, and you will find sweetness and abundance of peace. Savoury, sweet, and lasting fruit is gathered only in a dry and cold soil.

entries.chapterTitle: Though the road be plain and pleasant for men of good will, he who
entries.textEn: Though the road be plain and pleasant for men of good will, he who travels on it will travel little, and that with difficulty, if he be not possessed of great courage, physical strength, and resolute perseverance.

entries.chapterTitle: Feed not in the forbidden pastures, which are those of this life : the
entries.textEn: Feed not in the forbidden pastures, which are those of this life : the blessed are they who hungered and thirsted after justice, and it is they who are filled.

entries.chapterTitle: Verily he has overcome all things in whom the pleasures of them excite
entries.textEn: Verily he has overcome all things in whom the pleasures of them excite no joy, and the bitterness of them no sadness.

entries.chapterTitle: By fortitude the soul labours, practises virtue, and overcomes vice
entries.textEn: By fortitude the soul labours, practises virtue, and overcomes vice.

entries.chapterTitle: Let your heart be strong against everything that may attract you to
entries.textEn: Let your heart be strong against everything that may attract you to that which is not God, and be at home in the sufferings of Christ.

entries.chapterTitle: Rejoice in God always, for He is your salvation, and consider how good
entries.textEn: Rejoice in God always, for He is your salvation, and consider how good it is to suffer whatever may come from Him who is the true good.

entries.chapterTitle: If you incline to aridities and suffering for the love of God, He will
entries.textEn: If you incline to aridities and suffering for the love of God, He will esteem that in you of more value than all the spiritual visions, meditations, and consolations you may ever have.

entries.chapterTitle: Never, for good or for evil, suffer your heart to be otherwise than
entries.textEn: Never, for good or for evil, suffer your heart to be otherwise than calm in the affections of love ; that you may endure whatever may befal you.

entries.chapterTitle: We are not to measure our trials by ourselves, but ourselves by our trials
entries.textEn: We are not to measure our trials by ourselves, but ourselves by our trials.

entries.chapterTitle: If souls but knew the advantage of suffering and mortification for the
entries.textEn: If souls but knew the advantage of suffering and mortification for the attainment of great blessings, they would never seek for consolation anywhere.

entries.chapterTitle: If a soul has more patience under suffering, a greater endurance in the
entries.textEn: If a soul has more patience under suffering, a greater endurance in the absence of sweetness, that is a sign of greater progress in virtue.

entries.chapterTitle: The way of suffering is more secure and more profitable than that of
entries.textEn: The way of suffering is more secure and more profitable than that of joy and action. In suffering, the strength of God is given to the soul, while in joy and action it has to do with its own weakness and imperfections : in suffering also virtues are acquired and practised ; the soul is purified, and is rendered more prudent and cautious.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that is not tried and proved in temptations and afflictions
entries.textEn: The soul that is not tried and proved in temptations and afflictions can never attain unto wisdom, as it is written in the book Ecclesiasticus : 6 What doth he know that hath not been tried ?

entries.chapterTitle: The most perfect suffering brings with it the most perfect understanding
entries.textEn: The most perfect suffering brings with it the most perfect understanding. MODESTY.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul, by refraining from joy in the objects of sense, recovers
entries.textEn: The soul, by refraining from joy in the objects of sense, recovers itself from the distractions into which it has fallen through the excessive indulgence of the senses, and recollects itself in God: spirituality dnd the virtues it has acquired are also preserved and increased.

entries.chapterTitle: As the man who seeks pleasure in the things of sense, and rejoices in
entries.textEn: As the man who seeks pleasure in the things of sense, and rejoices in them, ought not, and deserves not, to be called by any other name than sensual, animal, and earthly, so he whose joy is beyond and above these things, merits the name of spiritual, heavenly, and divine.

entries.chapterTitle: If you will deny yourself one joy in the things of sense, our Lord will
entries.textEn: If you will deny yourself one joy in the things of sense, our Lord will repay you a hundred-fold in this life spiritually and temporally ; and for one joy indulged in the things of sense, you shall have a hundred sorrows and afflictions.

entries.chapterTitle: All the functions and powers of his senses, who no longer lives after
entries.textEn: All the functions and powers of his senses, who no longer lives after the flesh, are directed to Divine contemplation.

entries.chapterTitle: Though the goods of sense may deserve to be somewhat rejoiced in when
entries.textEn: Though the goods of sense may deserve to be somewhat rejoiced in when they help a man to raise his thoughts to God, yet this is so uncertain that in general they do a man more harm than good.

entries.chapterTitle: Until a man shall have so habituated his senses to the purgation from
entries.textEn: Until a man shall have so habituated his senses to the purgation from sensible joy, that all things raise him up to God, he must refrain from all joy in them, in order that he may wean his soul from the life of sense. SILENCE.

entries.chapterTitle: The Father uttered one Word;
entries.textEn: The Father uttered one Word; that Word is His Son : and He utters Him for ever in everlasting silence, and the soul to hear It must be silent.

entries.chapterTitle: That which we most require for our spiritual growth is the silence of
entries.textEn: That which we most require for our spiritual growth is the silence of the desire and of the tongue before God, Who is so high : the language He most listens to is that of silent love.

entries.chapterTitle: Speak little;
entries.textEn: Speak little; and do not meddle in matters when you are not desired to do so.

entries.chapterTitle: Complain of no one: ask for nothing, but if it should be necessary to
entries.textEn: Complain of no one: ask for nothing, but if it should be necessary to ask, do so in few words.

entries.chapterTitle: Abstain from contradiction : on no account let your words be other than pure
entries.textEn: Abstain from contradiction : on no account let your words be other than pure.

entries.chapterTitle: Let your language be offensive to none ;
entries.textEn: Let your language be offensive to none ; let it be about matters such as will cause you no trouble if everybody knew of them.

entries.chapterTitle: Preserve your spirit in peace, lovingly attentive to God : and when you
entries.textEn: Preserve your spirit in peace, lovingly attentive to God : and when you must speak, do so calmly and peaceably.

entries.chapterTitle: Be silent about what God may say to you, remembering the words of
entries.textEn: Be silent about what God may say to you, remembering the words of Scripture : ' My secret to me.

entries.chapterTitle: Never forget that of every word uttered without the direction of
entries.textEn: Never forget that of every word uttered without the direction of obedience, God will require a strict account.

entries.chapterTitle: Intercourse with people beyond what is strictly necessary, and required
entries.textEn: Intercourse with people beyond what is strictly necessary, and required by reason, has never been good for any man, however holy he may have been.

entries.chapterTitle: It is .impossible to make progress otherwise than by doing and
entries.textEn: It is .impossible to make progress otherwise than by doing and suffering everything in silence.

entries.chapterTitle: For growth in virtue, the important thing is to be silent, and to work
entries.textEn: For growth in virtue, the important thing is to be silent, and to work : conversation distracts, silence and work bring recollection.

entries.chapterTitle: The moment a person understands what is told him for his good, there is
entries.textEn: The moment a person understands what is told him for his good, there is no necessity for him to ask for further direction, nor to speak about it, but to act upon it sincerely in silence carefully, in humility, charity, and contempt of self.

entries.chapterTitle: I have understood that the soul which is ready for talking and the
entries.textEn: I have understood that the soul which is ready for talking and the commerce of the world is but little attentive to God : for if it were otherwise, it would withdraw itself at once into silence within, and avoid all conversation whatever.

entries.chapterTitle: It is the will of God that the soul should delight in Him, rather than
entries.textEn: It is the will of God that the soul should delight in Him, rather than in any created thing, however useful or necessary it may be to it.

entries.chapterTitle: The first thing the soul must have in order to attain to the knowledge
entries.textEn: The first thing the soul must have in order to attain to the knowledge of God is the knowledge of itself.

entries.chapterTitle: God is more pleased with certain actions, however few they may be, done
entries.textEn: God is more pleased with certain actions, however few they may be, done in silence and in secret, and without any desire that men might see them, than with a thousand grand actions undertaken with the intention of their becoming known to men.

entries.chapterTitle: The secrecy of conscience is broken when a man reveals to others the
entries.textEn: The secrecy of conscience is broken when a man reveals to others the blessings he has received: the reward of his actions is the praise of men.

entries.chapterTitle: The wise Spirit of God Who dwells in humble souls inclines them to keep
entries.textEn: The wise Spirit of God Who dwells in humble souls inclines them to keep His treasures in secret, and to make visible their imperfections.

entries.chapterTitle: Perfection consists not in those virtues which everyone recognises in
entries.textEn: Perfection consists not in those virtues which everyone recognises in himself, but in those which God approves of. And as His approval is hidden from the eyes of men, no one has any reason to presume, but rather much whereof to be afraid.

entries.chapterTitle: God, when He gives His love to a soul, regards not its greatness in
entries.textEn: God, when He gives His love to a soul, regards not its greatness in itself, but rather the greatness of its contempt of self, and its humility.

entries.chapterTitle: What you most seek, and most anxiously desire, you will never find if
entries.textEn: What you most seek, and most anxiously desire, you will never find if you seek it of yourself, not even in the most profound contemplation ; but only in deep humility and submission of heart.

entries.chapterTitle: If you will glory in yourself, cast away everything not your own : what
entries.textEn: If you will glory in yourself, cast away everything not your own : what remains will be nothing, and it is nothing you should glory in.

entries.chapterTitle: Do not despise others because, as it seems to you, they do not possess
entries.textEn: Do not despise others because, as it seems to you, they do not possess the virtues you thought they had: they may be pleasing to God for other reasons which you cannot discover.

entries.chapterTitle: Never excuse yourself : listen calmly to the reprimand and consider it
entries.textEn: Never excuse yourself : listen calmly to the reprimand and consider it to come from God.

entries.chapterTitle: Look upon it as a special mercy of God, that people ever speak kindly
entries.textEn: Look upon it as a special mercy of God, that people ever speak kindly to you : you do not deserve it.

entries.chapterTitle: Make neither much nor little of him who may be against you, and strive
entries.textEn: Make neither much nor little of him who may be against you, and strive always to please God. Pray that His will may be done, and love Him much, for that is your duty.

entries.chapterTitle: Love to be unknown to yourself and others: never regard the good nor
entries.textEn: Love to be unknown to yourself and others: never regard the good nor the evil of others.

entries.chapterTitle: Never forget the life to come
entries.textEn: Never forget the life to come. Consider how many in heaven are great, and in great glory, who in their own eyes were of no account, humble and poor.

entries.chapterTitle: In order to mortify really the desire of honour out of which so many
entries.textEn: In order to mortify really the desire of honour out of which so many other desires proceed, you will do those things which will bring you into contempt, and you will wish others to do the same : you will speak disparagiugly of yourself and you will contrive that others may do so too : you will think humbly and contemptuously of yourself, and you will wish others to do so also.

entries.chapterTitle: Humility and submission to your spiritual director, disclosing to him
entries.textEn: Humility and submission to your spiritual director, disclosing to him all that passes in your intercourse with God, will bring light, rest, contentment, and security.

entries.chapterTitle: Virtue consists not in apprehensions of, and feelings about God,
entries.textEn: Virtue consists not in apprehensions of, and feelings about God, however sublime they may be, nor in any personal experiences of this kind, but, on the contrary, in that which is not matter of feeling at all, in great humility, contempt of self, and of all that belongs to us profoundly rooted in the soul.

entries.chapterTitle: All visions, revelations, and impressions of heaven, however much the
entries.textEn: All visions, revelations, and impressions of heaven, however much the spiritual man may esteem them, are not equal in worth to the least act of humility : for this brings forth the fruits of charity, which never esteems nor thinks well of self, but only of others.

entries.chapterTitle: The communications which come really from God, have this property, that
entries.textEn: The communications which come really from God, have this property, that they humble and exalt the soul at the same time, for in the way of the Spirit to descend is to ascend, and to ascend is to descend.

entries.chapterTitle: When God communicates His gifts and graces to the soul, He excites in
entries.textEn: When God communicates His gifts and graces to the soul, He excites in it a repugnance to accept honours and distinctions, but in the way of humility and self-abasement, He gives it ease and readiness.

entries.chapterTitle: God hates to see men ready to accept dignities, even when it is His
entries.textEn: God hates to see men ready to accept dignities, even when it is His will that they should accept them, but it is not His will that they should do so eagerly and promptly.

entries.chapterTitle: When the devil speaks, he makes men ready and eager to accept
entries.textEn: When the devil speaks, he makes men ready and eager to accept dignities, but he makes them reject humiliations and self-abasement. VANITY.

entries.chapterTitle: He who loves superiorities and dignities, or the indulgence of his
entries.textEn: He who loves superiorities and dignities, or the indulgence of his desires, stands before God, not as a son who is free, but as one of mean condition, the slave of his passions.

entries.chapterTitle: The soul that is not humble, the devil most easily deludes, and makes
entries.textEn: The soul that is not humble, the devil most easily deludes, and makes it believe a thousand lies.

entries.chapterTitle: There are many Christians in our day who have certain virtues, and who
entries.textEn: There are many Christians in our day who have certain virtues, and who do great things, but all of no use to them in the matter of everlasting life, merely because they do not keep in view the honour and glory of God alone, but rather the empty satisfaction of their own will.

entries.chapterTitle: Empty joy in our good works is always attended by a great esteem of
entries.textEn: Empty joy in our good works is always attended by a great esteem of them : out of this comes boasting, and other faults such as we see in the Pharisee in the gospel.

entries.chapterTitle: Such is the misery of the children of men, that so far as I can see,
entries.textEn: Such is the misery of the children of men, that so far as I can see, the greater part of their good works done in public are either sinful or worthless, or imperfect and defective in the sight of God, because men will not detach themselves from self-interest and from human respect.

entries.chapterTitle: 0 souls created for, and called unto, a dignity so great! what are you
entries.textEn: 0 souls created for, and called unto, a dignity so great! what are you doing, what is it that detains you? O miserable blindness of the children of Adam, who in a light so great are blind, and to such an invitation deaf! While they seek after greatness and honour they are themselves miserable and base, and of such blessings unworthy.

entries.chapterTitle: If rejoicing in riches can be made in any way endurable, it is when men
entries.textEn: If rejoicing in riches can be made in any way endurable, it is when men spend and use them in the service of God ; there is no other way of making them profitable : the same principle applies to all other temporal goods, titles, rank, and office.

entries.chapterTitle: The spiritual man must be very careful of the beginnings of joy in
entries.textEn: The spiritual man must be very careful of the beginnings of joy in temporal things, lest from little it should become great, increasing from one degree to another; out of slight beginnings great evils result. One spark is enough to set a mountain on fire.

entries.chapterTitle: However small an attachment may be, be not too confident that you can
entries.textEn: However small an attachment may be, be not too confident that you can cut it off at any time, but cut it off at once : for if you have not the courage to destroy it when it is but beginning, how can you presume upon success when it has taken root and grown ?

entries.chapterTitle: He who turns aside from what is little, will not stumble over what is large
entries.textEn: He who turns aside from what is little, will not stumble over what is large. Little matters cause great evils. because the fences and walls of the heart are broken down when they enter in ; for the proverb says : he who has begun his work has accomplished the half of it.

entries.chapterTitle: Joy darkens the judgment as a cloud, for there can be no rejoicing in
entries.textEn: Joy darkens the judgment as a cloud, for there can be no rejoicing in created things without the attachment of the will. The negation and purgation of this joy leaves the judgment clear as the sky when the mist has been scattered.

entries.chapterTitle: He who is detached is not molested when he prays, nor at any other
entries.textEn: He who is detached is not molested when he prays, nor at any other time, and so without wasting his time he gains with ease great spiritual treasures. avarice.

entries.chapterTitle: Although temporal goods are not, in themselves, necessarily, occasions
entries.textEn: Although temporal goods are not, in themselves, necessarily, occasions of sin, yet ordinarily, by reason of our frailty, the heart of man sets its affections upon them, and falls away from God, which is sin : for this reason the wise man saith : the rich shall not be free from sin.

entries.chapterTitle: The things of this world neither occupy nor injure the soul ;
entries.textEn: The things of this world neither occupy nor injure the soul ; it is not they that enter into it, but rather the will, and the desire of them, which dwell within it.

entries.chapterTitle: Our Lord Jesus Christ, in the gospel, calls riches thorns, giving us to
entries.textEn: Our Lord Jesus Christ, in the gospel, calls riches thorns, giving us to understand that he who sets his will upon them shall be wounded by sin.

entries.chapterTitle: It is vanity to desire to have children, as some do, who weary the
entries.textEn: It is vanity to desire to have children, as some do, who weary the world with their fretting for them : they know not if their children will be good, and servants of God : neither do they know whether the pleasure they expect from them may not be turned into disquietude, pain, and trouble.

entries.chapterTitle: The covetous man runs to and fro within the limits of the chain by
entries.textEn: The covetous man runs to and fro within the limits of the chain by which his heart is bound, and with all his efforts can scarcely set himself free, even for a moment, from the bondage of his thoughts, running incessantly hither and thither within the length of the chain that binds him.

entries.chapterTitle: Consider how very necessary it is for you to set your face against
entries.textEn: Consider how very necessary it is for you to set your face against yourself, and walk in the way of penance, if you would attain to perfection.

entries.chapterTitle: If any one tempts you with lax opinions, and should even confirm them
entries.textEn: If any one tempts you with lax opinions, and should even confirm them by miracles, trust him not : but rely rather upon penance and perfect detachment from creatures.

entries.chapterTitle: God in the old law commanded that the altar of sacrifice should be empty within
entries.textEn: God in the old law commanded that the altar of sacrifice should be empty within. This is to teach us that the soul, which is to become an altar worthy of His Majesty, should be emptied of all things.

entries.chapterTitle: One desire only does God allow, and suffer in his presence within the
entries.textEn: One desire only does God allow, and suffer in his presence within the soul -- the desire of keeping the law perfectly, and carrying the cross of Christ. It is not said, in the sacred writings, that God commanded anything to be laid up in the ark with the manna except the book of the law and the rod of Moses, a type of the cross of Christ.

entries.chapterTitle: That soul which has no other aim than the perfect observance of the law
entries.textEn: That soul which has no other aim than the perfect observance of the law of our Lord, and the carrying of the cross of Christ, will be a true ark containing the true manna, which is God.

entries.chapterTitle: If you wish devotion to be born in your heart, the love of God to grow,
entries.textEn: If you wish devotion to be born in your heart, the love of God to grow, together with the desire for divine things, cleanse your soul from every desire and self-seeking, so that nothing of the kind remain with you. For as a sick man, freed from the evil humours which troubled him, feels instantly returning health and a taste for his food, so shall you recover your health in God if you rid yourself of your spiritual disorders : and if this be not done, whatever you may do, you will make no progress.

entries.chapterTitle: Live in this world as if God and your soul only were in it;
entries.textEn: Live in this world as if God and your soul only were in it; so shall your heart be never made captive by any earthly thing.

entries.chapterTitle: Do not weary yourself to no purpose : do not seek spiritual joy and
entries.textEn: Do not weary yourself to no purpose : do not seek spiritual joy and sweetness, unless it be by denying yourself in that which you aim at.

entries.chapterTitle: Be interiorly detached from all things, and do not set your affection
entries.textEn: Be interiorly detached from all things, and do not set your affection upon any temporal thing, and your soul will gather in a harvest of blessings beyond its comprehension.

entries.chapterTitle: The goods of God, which are beyond all measure, can be contained only
entries.textEn: The goods of God, which are beyond all measure, can be contained only in an empty and solitary heart.

entries.chapterTitle: So far as it lies in your power, refuse nothing asked of you, though
entries.textEn: So far as it lies in your power, refuse nothing asked of you, though you may have need of it yourself.

entries.chapterTitle: He will never attain to perfection who will not labour to be satisfied
entries.textEn: He will never attain to perfection who will not labour to be satisfied with this : that all his natural and spiritual desires should be satisfied in the absence of everything which is not God. This is most necessary for an abiding peace and tranquillity of spirit.

entries.chapterTitle: Let your soul be always ordered by a desire not for that which is easy,
entries.textEn: Let your soul be always ordered by a desire not for that which is easy, but for that which is most difficult ; not for that which is most pleasant, but for that which is most unpleasant ; not for that which is elevated and precious, but for that which is vile and despised ; not for great things, but for little things ; not to seek for anything, but to seek for nothing ; not for that which is best, but for that which is worst; desiring to enter, for the love of Jesus, upon detachment, emptiness, and poverty in everything of this world.

entries.chapterTitle: If you will cleanse your soul of strange possessions and desires, you
entries.textEn: If you will cleanse your soul of strange possessions and desires, you will understand all things spiritually ; and if you will restrain yourself from setting your heart upon them, you will rejoice truly in them, and understand them certainly.

entries.chapterTitle: All people will be your servants, and all things will minister to you,
entries.textEn: All people will be your servants, and all things will minister to you, if only you will forget them and yourself.

entries.chapterTitle: You will never have to do with necessities greater than those to which
entries.textEn: You will never have to do with necessities greater than those to which you made your heart yield itself : for the poor in spirit are most happy and joyous in a state of privation ; and he who has set his heart upon nothing, finds fulness everywhere.

entries.chapterTitle: The poor in spirit give generously all they have, and their pleasure
entries.textEn: The poor in spirit give generously all they have, and their pleasure consists in being thus deprived of everything for God's sake, and out of love to their neighbour, ordering all things by the laws of virtue.

entries.chapterTitle: Poverty of spirit looks to the substance of devotion, and makes use
entries.textEn: Poverty of spirit looks to the substance of devotion, and makes use only of what is sufficient for it : weary of the multiplicity and curiosity of visible means.

entries.chapterTitle: A soul withdrawn from exterior things, detached from its own will, even
entries.textEn: A soul withdrawn from exterior things, detached from its own will, even in divine things, will not be raised by prosperity nor subdued by adversity.

entries.chapterTitle: The poor that are naked shall be clothed : and the soul that will strip
entries.textEn: The poor that are naked shall be clothed : and the soul that will strip itself of all its desires, likings, and dislikings, God will clothe with His own purity. His own joy, and His own will.

entries.chapterTitle: The love of God in a pure and simple soul, detached from every desire,
entries.textEn: The love of God in a pure and simple soul, detached from every desire, is frequently in act.

entries.chapterTitle: Restrain your desires, and you will find that which your heart longs
entries.textEn: Restrain your desires, and you will find that which your heart longs for: how can you tell that your desire is according to the will of God?

entries.chapterTitle: If you desire to have your soul in peace and comfort, and to serve God
entries.textEn: If you desire to have your soul in peace and comfort, and to serve God in truth, do not rest satisfied with what you have done in the way of self-denial, for it may be that on the new road you have entered, you may find yourself as much hindered, or even more than you were, but give up everything that you have.

entries.chapterTitle: If you fail in the practice of self-denial, which is the sum and root
entries.textEn: If you fail in the practice of self-denial, which is the sum and root of virtue : every other way is but beating the air, and you will make no progress, notwithstanding great meditations and communications.

entries.chapterTitle: Not only do temporal goods, the delights and the tastes of sense,
entries.textEn: Not only do temporal goods, the delights and the tastes of sense, hinder and thwart the way of God, but spiritual delights and consolations also, if sought for, or clung to eagerly, disturb the way of virtue.

entries.chapterTitle: Such is the nature of our vain concupiscence that it clings to
entries.textEn: Such is the nature of our vain concupiscence that it clings to everything: like the dry-rot, which wastes away what is sound, it has its way both in what is good and what is bad.

entries.chapterTitle: O Lord God, my Love, if Thou art still mindful of my sins, and will not
entries.textEn: O Lord God, my Love, if Thou art still mindful of my sins, and will not grant my petitions, Thy will be done, for that is my chief desire. Show Thou Thy goodness and mercy, and Thou shalt be known by them. If it be that Thou art waiting for me to do good works, that in them Thou mayest grant my petition, do Thou give them and work them in me : send also the penalties which Thou wilt accept, and do Thou inflict them. But if Thou art not waiting for my good works ; what art Thou waiting for, O Most Merciful Lord ? why tarriest Thou? For if at last it must be grace and mercy, and I pray for it in Thy Son, do Thou accept my worthless offering, according to Thy will, and give me this good also according to Thy will. O Lord, Omnipotent, my spirit has fainted within me because it has forgotten to feed upon Thee. I knew Thee not, O my Lord, when I went after vanity. Who can free himself from base and mean ways, if Thou, O my God, wilt not lift him up to Thee in pure love ? Thou hastenest joyfully and lovingly, O Lord, to raise up him who has offended Thee, but I make no haste to honour and raise him up who has offended me. How shall a man raise himself up to Thee, for he is born and bred in misery, if Thou wilt not lift him up with the hand that made him ? O Lord, omnipotent, if the shadow of the power of Thy justice in earthly sovereigns who govern and rule the nations can do so much, what must be Thy omnipotent justice, dealing with the just man and the sinner ? O Lord my God, Thou art not estranged from him who does not estrange himself from Thee. How is it that men say thou art absent? O Lord my God, who is there that seeks Thee in pure and true love, who does not find Thee to be the joy of his will ? It is Thou who art the first to show Thyself, going forth to meet those who desire to meet Thee. Thou wilt not take away from me, O my God, what Thou hast once said to me in Thy Only Begotten Son Jesus Christ, in Whom Thou dost tell me all I desire. I will therefore rejoice. Thou wilt not tarry if I wait for Thee. Wait in hope then, O my soul, for from henceforth thou mayest love God in thy heart. The heavens are mine, the earth is mine, and the nations are mine : mine are the just, and the sinners are mine : mine are the Angels, the Mother of God, and all things are mine : God Himself is mine and for me, because Christ is mine, and all for me. What dost thou then ask for, what dost thou seek for, O my soul ? All is thine, all is for thee, do not take less, nor rest with the crumbs which fall from the table of thy Father. Go forth and exult in thy glory, hide thyself in it, and rejoice, and thou shalt obtain all the desires of thy heart. 0 sweetest love of God, too little known; he who has found thee is at rest : let everything be changed, O my God, that we may rest in Thee. Everywhere with Thee, O my God, everywhere all things with Thee as I wish. O my Love, all for Thee, nothing for me : nothing for Thee, everything for me. All sweetness and delight for Thee, none for me : all bitterness and trouble for me, none for Thee. O my God, how sweet to me Thy presence, who art the Supreme Good. I will draw near to Thee in silence, and will uncover Thy feet, that it may please Thee to unite me to Thyself, making my soul Thy bride : I will rejoice in nothing till I am in thine arms. O Lord, I beseech Thee, leave me not for a moment, because I know not the value of my soul.
